source_user: Advanced cluster case GDS-65: Evaluate GPUDirect Storage for checkpoint and dataset I/O in distributed training. Variant 65 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate storage throughput from GPU DMA, validate filesystem and kernel support, measure queue depth and tail latency, compare CPU-staged I/O, and test restart consistency after interruption. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume an authorized, isolated multi-node pilot, disposable copies, and an unchanged CPU-staged fallback; treat platform capability as unknown until measured. First inventory GPU, NVMe/storage, PCIe, NUMA, process/I/O affinity, filesystem and mount support, kernel/driver/runtime versions, container permissions, checkpoint format, request size, concurrency, queue depth, cache/compression state, synchronization, and durability semantics. Hypothesis: once direct GPU-DMA activation is independently evidenced, GDS lowers end-to-end checkpoint/dataset stall or host CPU versus a matched CPU-staged control without violating preregistered p99 latency, error, integrity, or restart limits. Measure storage and GPU-DMA throughput separately (GB/s), end-to-end and stall time, host CPU%, GPU idle%, queue depth, p50/p95/p99 latency, retries, errors, checksum mismatches, and restart recovery time with synchronized timestamps and confidence intervals. Use cold/warm-cache, compression, request-size, queue-depth, and contention controls; verify data hashes and resumed training state after interruption or node loss. Roll back to CPU staging immediately on integrity failure, repeated errors, or a predeclared p99/stall regression, and retain logs and configuration before changing one factor at a time.

Separate storage, transport, and application metrics. Stop and revert if integrity checks fail or p99 latency, error rate, or stall exceeds the registered rollback threshold; evidence must include synchronized traces and exact versions.

Change one reversible factor at a time, reproduce across nodes, and test interruption/node-loss recovery. Immediately roll back to CPU staging and quarantine outputs on checksum mismatch, unrecoverable restart state, or repeated errors; evidence_required includes logs, traces, configs, hashes, and before/after measurements.

Automate matched controls, repeated trials, checksums, interruption and node-failure recovery, and emit explicit units and uncertainty. Never overwrite source data; use a new output location and approval gate. Abort and invoke the unchanged CPU fallback on permission errors, checksum mismatch, or predeclared latency/error regression; retain evidence for review.
